imageNote: This lesson is more conceptual than the rest of the chapter, per the assignment brief, so the search widened beyond a single 'build' tutorial. The best real source turned out to still be Tableau's own official documentation: 'Choose the Right Chart Type for Your Data' (help.tableau.com/current/pro/desktop/en-us/what_chart_example.htm) organizes chart selection by seven analytical goals (change over time, correlation, magnitude, deviation, distribution, ranking, part-to-whole, spatial), each with its own small real illustration. Two of those seven header graphics are used here as real, unaltered screenshots. A broader web search for third-party 'chart chooser' diagrams (the Extreme Presentation / Andrew Abela-style decision diagrams referenced across data-viz blogs) turned up only non-Tableau-branded, generic diagrams whose exact original source and license were unclear — rather than risk misattributing one, this lesson's decision framework is instead presented as an original LTV-authored steps summary of Tableau's own seven-category framework, honestly labeled as original, not a screenshot.
